attempted_claim: Let d_LP be the universal cusp-density lower bound for hyperbolic alternating knots proved by Lackenby-Purcell (Geometry and Topology 20 (2016), Theorem 1.1 and corollary on cusp density). Restricted to hyperbolic alternating Montesinos knots of fixed Montesinos length 4, is d_LP best possible? Decide by certified cusp-volume and volume computation over an explicit length-4 Montesinos sequence with twist number tending to infinity: either exhibit a sequence K_n in this subfamily whose cusp densities converge to within 0.01 of d_LP, proving sharpness for Montesinos knots, or prove an improved uniform bound d_LP + epsilon with explicit epsilon >= 0.02 valid for all length-4 alternating Montesinos knots via octahedral-decoration counting. A complete answer either establishes the extremal law approaching d_LP or establishes the stated Montesinos gap; finite-window min-max fitting without a universal constant does not count.
claim_type: sharpness-or-gap extremal law for universal bound in subfamily
decisive_failure: No interval-certified hyperbolic-geometry computation stack was available in the workspace, so no admissible cusp-volume or volume enclosures could be produced; published two-sided twist-number bounds alone yield only a vacuous density window and cannot decide either target horn. The gap horn additionally requires a new uniform octahedral-counting theorem improving the known area constant by about eighteen orders of magnitude, which is beyond a single bounded pass.
